speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You have a painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg; to begin my evaluation, how long have you had this lesion, and what does it look like specifically?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Cutaneous Leishmaniasis. The patient's history of an ant bite (likely sand fly), a painful ulcerative lesion on the leg, and significant immunosuppression due to Crohn's disease (on corticosteroids) and uveitis strongly suggest an opportunistic parasitic infection. I will confirm this by requesting a tissue biopsy for microscopy and culture.
